title: Sundown runtime — ephemeral TODOs and notes
content:
Sundown shift scratchpad (personal) — quick capture of triage, hypotheses, and tiny experiments

Context
- Night shift: triaging the p99 jump on small requests (<=128 tokens) that started after last kernel patch.
- Short goal: capture reproducible repro, narrow hypothesis, and schedule 1-2 small fixes to try tomorrow morning.
- Keep this doc terse; mostly notes to self and commands to rerun.

Observed behavior (summary)
- Baseline: steady p99 ~12ms for <128 token requests pre-patch. After patch X (merged 2026-03-10) p99 intermittently spikes to 45–90ms for ~1–4% of requests.
- Spike pattern: correlated with sudden increase in context-switches on heavy multi-tenant hosts. Not all hosts affected.
- Affected path: decoder-only LLMs using KV-cache and continuous batching.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked)
1) NUMA/affinity regression: new allocator path altered CPU affinity for kv-cache evictions causing cross-socket memory traffic under bursts.
2) Lock contention: new hot-path tracing adds a contended atomic around cache lookup on certain sequences.
3) Scheduler interaction: continuous-batcher idle->active ramp behaves poorly with the new backoff timing, creating micro-queues that block a worker thread briefly.

Quick experiments to run (commands)
- Reproduce locally with microbench:
  ./scripts/microbench_kv --model redwood-mini --seq 128 --concurrency 64 --duration 120 --trace-locks > out1.log
- Perf to capture syscall/context-switch spikes:
  sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 60 && sudo perf script | ./scripts/stack-collapse.pl > perf.folded
- Force NUMA pinning to test hypothesis 1:
  numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 ./runtime_binary --kv-evict=on

What I ran tonight (notes)
- microbench_kv with --concurrency 64: reproduced p99 ~68ms on local 2-socket dev box when running 8 other background processes.
- perf showed occasional kernel preemptions and high context-switch rate aligned with the p99 spikes.
- Added a quick compile with tracing disabled (revert-of-flag) and retested: spikes reduced but not eliminated. Suggests tracing amplifies but is not sole cause.

Small reproducible script (for the morning)
- Steps to reproduce in CI-like runner:
  1) Start 2-socket VM (2 numa nodes).
  2) Start 4 helper load generators pinned to node1.
  3) Start runtime pinned to node0/node1 variants with env KV_EVICT_DEBUG=1.
  4) Run microbench_kv at concurrency 64 for 3 minutes and collect traces/perf.

Things to try next (prioritized)
- P0: Toggle NUMA pinning in production canary (node-local vs default) for 1 host group; watch p99 delta. (Need SRE signoff).
- P1: Roll back last tracing flag change on a canary to confirm amplification hypothesis.
- P1: Add lightweight per-request histogram (atomic-free) to measure latency components (queue wait vs processing).
- P2: Replace atomic increment in cache lookup with non-blocking per-shard counters (micro-optim).

Notes-to-self (quick)
- If NUMA test shows improvement, prepare small patch to set default allocator node affinity for kv-cache.
- If rolling back tracing fixes it, we should redesign the tracing path to be sampled (1/100) and avoid atomics on hot path.
- If neither helps, instrument batcher wake-up timing and log time-in-queue per-request to see micro-queueing.

Commands & snippets to paste in tickets
- perf command used: sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pgrep runtime_binary) -- sleep 120
- microbench invocation: ./scripts/microbench_kv --model redwood-mini --seq 128 --concurrency 64 --duration 180 --log-level debug

Open questions (for triage meeting)
- Which hosts saw the kernel patch X? cross-check with release history and host tagging.
- Did SRE change VM image/kernel config last week? Ask infra for a diff.
- Any other teams enabling tracing flags around same time? Check feature flags dashboard.

Quick timeline/next actions (myself + SRE)
- Tonight: drop a comment on RINF-3128 with perf fold + microbench logs (DONE).
- Tomorrow morning: 8:30am run NUMA canary with SRE (tag SRE-oncall).
- Tomorrow afternoon: if canary shows >20% improvement at p99, prepare upstream allocator-affinity patch and open a short PR.

Mental checklist before shift end
- [x] Save perf output to /tmp/sundown-perf-20260312.folded
- [x] Upload microbench logs to ticket (RINF-3128)
- [ ] Post a short summary in #runtime-night-handoff channel before 23:45 PT
- [ ] Add per-request histogram ticket to backlog (label: perf-low-effort)

Random friction notes (brain dump)
- Local dev box runs different kernel (5.15) vs prod (5.19). Might matter for context-switch metrics.
- CI images currently default to single-numa binding; need an image variant for two-node tests. Create ticket for CI infra to add 2-numa test image.

Small todo list (one-liners)
- Create canary plan + SRE runbook (10–15 mins).
- Draft allocator-affinity patch skeleton.
- Add sampling to tracing path (config flag).
- Add microbench to night-runner job and alert on p99>40ms

End of shift notes
- Logged everything to RINF-3128. Low-confidence cause is tracing; high-confidence cause likely NUMA affinity in combination with increased syscall churn.
- Sleep now, pick up at 08:30 with SRE and reproduce on canary.

— E.C.
